next_directions.name: conditional_factor_covariance
next_directions.proposal: Predict a diagonal variance plus low-rank factor loadings; train a per-date Gaussian likelihood using a Woodbury/Cholesky calculation. Compare against the existing independent Gaussian head and test loss/gradients against a dense MultivariateNormal. Forecast features never receive future returns.
next_directions.evidence: Dense likelihood/gradient comparisons and two-market GPU smoke checks pass. First CSI300 rank-4 raw-return model improves validation RankIC 0.07067 -> 0.08009 versus rank 0, but its portfolio metrics trail existing leaders.
next_directions.additional_evidence: Raw-excess targets show mixed portfolio results: CSI300 rank 4 without penalty has validation AR -0.01992; SP500 rank 4 with penalty 0.1 has AR 0.15626 but STD 0.28841. Ranking gains do not imply the required volatility and drawdown improvements.

next_directions.name: market_regime_risk_penalty
next_directions.status: implemented; two sets of 16 full static/adaptive controls, plus 14 SP500 follow-ups queued
next_directions.proposal: Scale the frozen variance penalty using the current date mean forecast variance; fit centering and scale only on selected training-date predictions, save them as checkpoint buffers, and compare with a constant penalty.
next_directions.evidence: 45 CPU tests pass; two-market GPU smoke checks and checkpoint recovery pass. CSI300 zero-penalty audit reproduces 143786 predictions exactly and all ten metrics within 2.9e-15. SP500 independent-risk fixed-alpha strength 0.5, penalty 0.05 has validation RankIC 0.04515, AR 0.22623, STD 0.22313 and MDD -0.15152; variance reduction remains insufficient to claim the research goal.

next_directions.name: top30_pair_loss
next_directions.status: implemented; six full matched controls completed
next_directions.proposal: Add a separately named ranking objective emphasizing the true training top 30 against other stocks. Preserve existing objectives for reproducibility. CSRankNorm training labels have std about 1 and range about [-1.73,1.73], so the existing >1 tail threshold is already active.
next_directions.evidence: Initial CSI300 Top30 objectives reduce validation RankIC and generally worsen drawdown relative to mixed-loss controls. Preserve these negative results; adding a portfolio-oriented loss does not by itself improve the portfolio.

next_directions.name: opportunity_conditioned_risk_penalty
next_directions.status: implemented; 14 full controls and 4 matched CSI300 seed checks completed; 52 CPU checks and two-market GPU scoring/recovery pass
next_directions.proposal: Compare forecast-risk scaling with the dispersion of the current alpha forecast, using only selected training-feature forecasts to fit any reference statistics. Retain fixed-alpha/static/regime controls; future returns must remain evaluation targets only. The goal is to preserve strong alpha opportunities while suppressing poorly differentiated high-risk dates.
next_directions.evidence: Early CSI300 opportunity strength 0.5 with static variance penalty 0.05 improves validation AR 0.22918 -> 0.25831 and Sharpe 1.14844 -> 1.26988; STD increases slightly. No holdout evidence.
next_directions.additional_evidence: Matched CSI300 three-seed opportunity avg_none AR 0.14788 -> 0.15332, STD 0.17136 -> 0.17048, MDD -0.15645 -> -0.15533; ICIR and RankICIR decrease slightly. SP500 RankIC gains often worsen volatility/drawdown.

next_directions.name: conditional_gaussian_mixture
next_directions.status: implemented; eighteen full controls and paired CSI300 seed ensembles complete
next_directions.proposal: Train a feature-conditioned mixture of Gaussian experts with a stable logsumexp mixture likelihood and the existing per-date ranking objective. Compare one component with the ordinary Gaussian head; compute scoring risk via total variance including between-expert dispersion. Fit numerical encoders on selected training features only, retain baseline evaluation and test guards.
next_directions.mechanism_note: The supplied MoE summary explicitly warns that squared loss of blended outputs does not establish expert specialization. Use mixture likelihood; do not label a shared-head local adaptation as a complete PRISM-VQ or historical-paper reproduction.
required_checks: Mixture NLL values and all gradients against torch.distributions.MixtureSameFamily on CPU
One-component reduction to the existing independent Gaussian loss
Two-market GPU smoke and checkpoint recovery
Full validation, calibration and seed robustness before any claim
next_directions.evidence: Two-component CSI300 seed 0 improves all ten validation metrics versus one component. Three-seed avg_none improves RankIC 0.07666 -> 0.08045, but AR declines 0.10765 -> 0.04328; portfolio benefit is not robust to the required ensemble rule.

next_directions.name: frozen_mixture_risk
next_directions.status: twelve matched controls complete; eight paired alpha-seed checks queued
next_directions.evidence: Both markets reproduce identical complete alpha predictions at zero penalty; all ten baseline metrics differ by at most 3.11e-15. Same alpha checkpoint, penalty 0.05 and baseline strategy for one/two/four components and static/regime scoring.
next_directions.result: CSI300 two-component static scoring improves AR with a small STD increase. SP500 one-component regime scoring is strongest within these controls; adding components is not consistently beneficial.

interpretation: The conditional mixture mean-score ensemble improves ranking but loses portfolio returns versus one component. Twelve matched frozen-risk controls show a small CSI300 two-component static benefit with slightly higher volatility; SP500 favors one component with risk-regime scaling. Eight paired alpha-seed checks are queued before trusting these seed-0 results. Full native history controls are running. Test remains sealed and the full baseline objective is unproven.
